rules.rule: Check for new medication in generalised rash
Check for drug rash markers of severity
rules.problem: Type, trigger and the 19 severity items are right, but the last two findings (Hyperpigmentation of skin, Macule of skin) are fixed-drug-eruption discriminators from the 'No' branch, not markers of severity, and sit under a task whose name says otherwise; they should be a separate task or the task renamed. Nothing invented.

rules.rule: Suspect drug rash: generalised rash after new medication
rules.problem: possible is right for 'Suspect'. The 3-month window is measured to the consultation rather than to the rash's appearance (c026); the language has no better form.

probable is right for 'fixed drug eruption likely'. Two weaknesses: (1) the page's single lesion description is split into two independent generic findings, so unrelated hyperpigmentation plus any macule fires it; (2) the page gives this only in the 'not needing urgent attention' / 'No' (not on ART, TB medication, co-trimoxazole or TPT) branch, and the rule drops both conditions. Neither is inventable content, and the 'often start as itchy patches with red edges' qualifier is rightly left optional.

rules.rule: Urgent: drug rash with markers of severity
rules.problem: Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention'; (and drug rash (or markers)) matches the box; every item traces to the box or footnote 2. SBP < 80 and SBP < 90 both present is redundant but harmless. Gap, not distortion: footnote 1 says 'shock likely' for SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, and no probable Shock rule encodes it.

summary: Nothing on this page was invented or misread: every red-box item, both BP thresholds, the temperature, the 3-month window and both diagnoses trace to the page with the right certainty. The weakest point is the fixed drug eruption rule, which splits 'dark coloured round flat spots' into two independent findings (Hyperpigmentation of skin AND Macule of skin) and ignores that the page reaches it only in the non-urgent, not-on-ART/TB/co-trimoxazole/TPT branch; those two findings are also filed under a check_for task named 'markers of severity'. Minor: the drug-rash onset window is measured to the consultation rather than to the rash's appearance, and footnote 1's 'shock likely' criteria have no probable Shock rule.
